front: What does it mean for two shapes to be **similar**?
back: Corresponding angles are equal and corresponding lengths are in the same ratio (the scale factor).

front: Scale factor $k$ from shape A to shape B
Three ways to show that two triangles are similar
back: Two pairs of equal angles; or all three pairs of sides in the same ratio; or two pairs of sides in the same ratio with equal included angles.

front: In triangle $ABC$, $DE \parallel BC$ with $D$ on $AB$, $E$ on $AC$. Which ratio gives the scale factor?
back: $\dfrac{AB}{AD}$: compare the whole side with the part, never $\dfrac{DB}{AD}$.

front: How do the masses of similar solids of the same material compare?
back: In the same ratio as their volumes: multiply by $k^3$.

Name three types of shape where any two are always similar.
back: Squares, circles and equilateral triangles (also any two regular polygons with the same number of sides).
